question:
Find the part of the sentence that contains an error.

 

Many employees (a)/ prefer to work at the home (b)/ these days (c)/ because of flexible timings. (d)
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. (b).

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Home" used in the sense of one's own place of living takes no article in fixed expressions such as at home, go home and stay home. So "at the home" must be "at home".

◦ Corrected sentence: Many employees prefer to work at home these days because of flexible timings.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Part (a) is correct — "Many employees" is a proper plural subject, with "many" followed by a plural noun.

 

• Part (c) is correct — "these days" is a proper adverbial phrase of time.

 

• Part (d) is correct — "because of flexible timings." is proper, with "because of" followed by a noun phrase.

 

NOTE

 

• no article: at home, go home, stay at home, work from home; with a specific reference: at the home of a friend.

question:
Find the part of the sentence that contains an error.

 

Milkha Singh was (a)/ a great athlete (b)/ of his time and (c)/ popularly known as Flying Sikh. (d)
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. (d).

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Nicknames and epithets used with "known as / called / named" take the definite article "the". So "Flying Sikh" must be "the Flying Sikh".

◦ Corrected sentence: Milkha Singh was a great athlete of his time and popularly known as the Flying Sikh.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Part (a) is correct — "Milkha Singh was" is proper, because the name of a person takes no article.

 

• Part (b) is correct — "a great athlete" is proper, with "a" used before the consonant sound of "great".

 

• Part (c) is correct — "of his time and" is a proper phrase joining two descriptions of the same person.

 

NOTE

 

• epithets take "the": the Iron Man of India, the Missile Man, the Flying Sikh, the Nightingale of India.

question:
Find the part of the sentence that contains an error.

 

On whole, (a)/ the trip was (b)/ enjoyable, (c)/ though it rained twice. (d)
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. (a).

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "On the whole" (= in general) is a fixed idiom, and it needs "the". So "On whole" must be "On the whole".

◦ Corrected sentence: On the whole, the trip was enjoyable, though it rained twice.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Part (b) is correct — "the trip was" is proper, with "the trip" as a specific journey.

 

• Part (c) is correct — "enjoyable," is a proper adjective after the linking verb "was".

 

• Part (d) is correct — "though it rained twice." is a proper clause of contrast, with the adverb "twice" correctly placed.

 

NOTE

 

• idioms with "the": on the whole, in the end, by the way, on the other hand, in the long run.

question:
Find the part of the sentence that contains an error.

 

My father reads (a)/ Hindu (b)/ every morning (c)/ before leaving for office. (d)
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. (b).

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The names of newspapers take the definite article "the". So "Hindu" must be "The Hindu".

◦ Corrected sentence: My father reads The Hindu every morning before leaving for office.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Part (a) is correct — "My father reads" is a proper singular subject and verb, with the possessive "My" used and no article.

 

• Part (c) is correct — "every morning" is a proper adverbial phrase, and "every" takes no article.

 

• Part (d) is correct — "before leaving for office." is proper, because "office" used for the place of work in general takes no article.

 

NOTE

 

• newspapers and books: the Hindu, the Times of India, the Statesman; holy books and documents: the Ramayana, the Gita, the Constitution.

question:
Find the part of the sentence that contains an error. If the sentence is free from error, select 'No error'.

 

The honesty (a)/ is the best policy (b)/ in every walk of life. (c)/ No error (d)
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. (a).

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Abstract nouns used in a general sense take no article. So "The honesty" must be "Honesty".

◦ Corrected sentence: Honesty is the best policy in every walk of life.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Part (b) is correct — "is the best policy" is proper, with "the" correctly used before the superlative "best".

 

• Part (c) is correct — "in every walk of life." is a proper idiomatic phrase, with no article needed after "every".

 

• Option (d) No error — cannot be selected, because "The" before "honesty" in part (a) is wrong.

 

NOTE

 

• Honesty is the best policy, Knowledge is power, Patience is a virtue (abstract nouns used generally take no article).

question:
Find the part of the sentence that contains an error.

 

Every writer needs (a)/ a notebook and (b)/ the quiet place (c)/ where he can think freely. (d)
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. (c).

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• When a noun stands for any one thing of a kind and not for a particular known one, it takes "a". The sentence speaks of what every writer needs, so "the quiet place" must be "a quiet place".

◦ Corrected sentence: Every writer needs a notebook and a quiet place where he can think freely.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Part (a) is correct — "Every writer needs" is proper, with "every" followed by a singular noun and the singular verb "needs".

 

• Part (b) is correct — "a notebook and" is proper, with "a" used before the consonant sound of "notebook".

 

• Part (d) is correct — "where he can think freely." is a proper relative clause, with "where" used for a place and the adverb "freely".

 

NOTE

 

• a place where (any such place) and the place where (one known place): Every child needs a place where he can play; This is the place where I was born.

question:
Find the part of the sentence that contains an error. If the sentence is free from error, select 'No error'.

 

The old godown was locked (a)/ at night, but it (b)/ caught the fire before dawn. (c)/ No error (d)
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. (c).

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Catch fire" (= begin to burn) is a fixed phrase and takes no article. So "caught the fire" must be "caught fire".

◦ Corrected sentence: The old godown was locked at night, but it caught fire before dawn.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Part (a) is correct — "The old godown was locked" is a proper passive verb, with "the" used for a specific godown.

 

• Part (b) is correct — "at night, but it" is proper, because "at night" is a fixed phrase without an article.

 

• Option (d) No error — cannot be selected, because "the" in "caught the fire" in part (c) is wrong.

 

NOTE

 

• fixed phrases without an article: catch fire, set fire to, on fire, take place, lose heart, learn by heart.

question:
Find the part of the sentence that contains an error.

 

The earth (a)/ takes 365 days to (b)/ complete a journey (c)/ around sun. (d)
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. (d).

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The sun is a unique object, so it takes the definite article "the". So "around sun" must be "around the sun".

◦ Corrected sentence: The earth takes 365 days to complete a journey around the sun.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Part (a) is correct — "The earth" is proper, with "the" used for a unique body.

 

• Part (b) is correct — "takes 365 days to" is a proper singular verb followed by an infinitive of purpose.

 

• Part (c) is correct — "complete a journey" is proper, with "a" used before the consonant sound of "journey".

 

NOTE

 

• the earth revolves around the sun, the moon revolves around the earth (unique bodies take "the"); but the names of planets take no article: Mars, Venus, Jupiter.

question:
Find the part of the sentence that contains an error.

 

The tourists (a)/ carried (b)/ a heavy luggage (c)/ to the station. (d)
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. (c).

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Luggage" is an uncountable noun, so it cannot be used with "a / an" or in the plural. So "a heavy luggage" must be "heavy luggage" (or "a heavy piece of luggage").

◦ Corrected sentence: The tourists carried heavy luggage to the station.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Part (a) is correct — "The tourists" is a proper plural subject.

 

• Part (b) is correct — "carried" is a proper simple past verb.

 

• Part (d) is correct — "to the station." is proper, with "the station" as a specific place.

 

NOTE

 

• uncountable nouns take no "a / an": luggage, furniture, information, advice, news, equipment; use a piece of: a piece of advice.

question:
Find the part of the sentence that contains an error.

 

New engine (a)/ designed by (b)/ our engineers (c)/ consumes less fuel. (d)
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. (a).

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• A singular countable noun cannot be used without an article. Here the engine is identified by the phrase "designed by our engineers", so it needs "the": "The new engine".

◦ Corrected sentence: The new engine designed by our engineers consumes less fuel.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Part (b) is correct — "designed by" is a proper past participle phrase describing the engine.

 

• Part (c) is correct — "our engineers" is a proper phrase, with the possessive "our" used and no article.

 

• Part (d) is correct — "consumes less fuel." is proper, with the singular verb "consumes" and "less" used before the uncountable noun "fuel".

 

NOTE

 

• singular countable noun + no determiner = error: The new engine / A new engine (not New engine); "the" when the noun is identified, "a / an" when it is new.

question:
Find the part of the sentence that contains an error.

 

After the crisis, (a)/ the manager (b)/ realised (c)/ importance of teamwork. (d)
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. (d).

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• When a noun such as "importance" is followed by an "of" phrase that specifies it, the noun takes "the". So "importance of teamwork" must be "the importance of teamwork".

◦ Corrected sentence: After the crisis, the manager realised the importance of teamwork.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Part (a) is correct — "After the crisis," is a proper introductory phrase, with "the crisis" as a specific event.

 

• Part (b) is correct — "the manager" is a proper singular subject.

 

• Part (c) is correct — "realised" is a proper simple past verb.

 

NOTE

 

• realise the importance of, understand the value of, know the meaning of (the + noun + "of" phrase).

question:
Find the part of the sentence that contains an error.

 

The clerk sent (a)/ the parcel to (b)/ the wrong address (c)/ by a mistake. (d)
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. (d).

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "By mistake" is a fixed adverbial phrase and takes no article. So "by a mistake" must be "by mistake".

◦ Corrected sentence: The clerk sent the parcel to the wrong address by mistake.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Part (a) is correct — "The clerk sent" is a proper singular subject with a simple past verb.

 

• Part (b) is correct — "the parcel to" is proper, with "the parcel" as a specific object.

 

• Part (c) is correct — "the wrong address" is proper, with "the" used before "wrong" and a singular noun.

 

NOTE

 

• no article: by mistake, by chance, by heart, by air, by hand; with "a": in a hurry, as a rule, at a glance.

question:
Find the part of the sentence that contains an error.

 

Anita speaks (a)/ the French fluently (b)/ and understands (c)/ German quite well. (d)
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. (b).

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The names of languages take no article. "The French" means the people of France, so "the French" must be "French".

◦ Corrected sentence: Anita speaks French fluently and understands German quite well.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Part (a) is correct — "Anita speaks" is a proper singular subject with a singular verb, and a personal name takes no article.

 

• Part (c) is correct — "and understands" is a proper compound verb, with "understands" agreeing with the singular subject.

 

• Part (d) is correct — "German quite well." is proper, because the name of a language takes no article and "quite" correctly modifies the adverb "well".

 

NOTE

 

• no article with languages and school subjects: speak English, learn Hindi, study history; the French (= the people of France) is a different meaning.

question:
Find the part of the sentence that contains an error.

 

The bill was (a)/ passed in the Lok Sabha (b)/ despite strong protests (c)/ from an opposition. (d)
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. (d).

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "The opposition" means the political parties opposed to the government, and it is a unique group, so it takes "the". So "an opposition" must be "the opposition".

◦ Corrected sentence: The bill was passed in the Lok Sabha despite strong protests from the opposition.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Part (a) is correct — "The bill was" is a proper singular passive subject and verb.

 

• Part (b) is correct — "passed in the Lok Sabha" is proper, with "the" used before the name of the House.

 

• Part (c) is correct — "despite strong protests" is proper, with a plural noun taking no article.

 

NOTE

 

• unique groups take "the": the opposition, the government, the press, the public, the media, the police.

question:
Find the part of the sentence that contains an error.

 

As rule, (a)/ the shop (b)/ opens at nine (c)/ on weekdays. (d)
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. (a).

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "As a rule" (= usually) is a fixed expression, and it needs "a". So "As rule" must be "As a rule".

◦ Corrected sentence: As a rule, the shop opens at nine on weekdays.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Part (b) is correct — "the shop" is a proper singular subject, with "the" used for a specific shop.

 

• Part (c) is correct — "opens at nine" is a proper singular verb with "at" before a clock time.

 

• Part (d) is correct — "on weekdays." is a proper prepositional phrase, with a plural noun taking no article.

 

NOTE

 

• idioms with "a": as a rule, in a hurry, at a glance, as a result, for a while, in a nutshell.

question:
Find the part of the sentence that contains an error.

 

The earlier (a)/ you start preparing, (b)/ more confident (c)/ you will feel. (d)
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. (c).

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• In the pattern "The + comparative … the + comparative", both clauses begin with "the". The second clause lacks it, so "more confident" must be "the more confident".

◦ Corrected sentence: The earlier you start preparing, the more confident you will feel.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Part (a) is correct — "The earlier" is a proper beginning, with "the" and the comparative "earlier".

 

• Part (b) is correct — "you start preparing," is proper, with the simple present used in the first clause and the gerund after "start".

 

• Part (d) is correct — "you will feel." is a proper future verb, with "feel" as a linking verb followed by an adjective.

 

NOTE

 

• The + comparative + subject + verb, the + comparative + subject + verb: The more you read, the more you learn; The sooner, the better.

question:
Find the part of the sentence that contains an error.

 

The soldiers (a)/ were honoured (b)/ for an exceptional courage (c)/ displayed in the battle. (d)
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. (c).

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Courage" is an abstract, uncountable noun, so it cannot be used with "an". Here it is specified by the phrase "displayed in the battle", so it takes "the": "the exceptional courage".

◦ Corrected sentence: The soldiers were honoured for the exceptional courage displayed in the battle.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Part (a) is correct — "The soldiers" is a proper plural subject.

 

• Part (b) is correct — "were honoured" is a proper plural passive verb, agreeing with "soldiers".

 

• Part (d) is correct — "displayed in the battle." is a proper past participle phrase, with "the battle" as a specific event.

 

NOTE

 

• abstract nouns never take "a / an": courage, bravery, honesty; they take "the" only when specified: the courage of the soldiers, the bravery shown by the boy.

question:
Find the part of the sentence that contains an error.

 

A MBA graduate (a)/ from a reputed college (b)/ has been appointed (c)/ to lead the new team. (d)
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. (a).

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The choice between "a" and "an" depends on the sound of the first letter as it is spoken. "MBA" is pronounced "em-bee-ay", which begins with a vowel sound, so it takes "an": "An MBA graduate".

◦ Corrected sentence: An MBA graduate from a reputed college has been appointed to lead the new team.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Part (b) is correct — "from a reputed college" is proper, with "a" used before the consonant sound of "reputed".

 

• Part (c) is correct — "has been appointed" is a proper singular present perfect passive verb.

 

• Part (d) is correct — "to lead the new team." is a proper infinitive of purpose, with "the new team" as a specific team.

 

NOTE

 

• abbreviations follow the sound of the first letter: an MBA, an MLA, an FIR, an SDM (vowel sounds); a BA, a CEO, a PhD (consonant sounds).

question:
Choose the most suitable option to replace the highlighted part of the sentence.

 

Rohan is an honest and hardworking officer who has served the department for years.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. No substitution required.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The sentence is correct as it stands. "Honest" begins with a vowel sound (the "h" is silent), so "an honest and hardworking officer" is correct, and the single article covers both adjectives that describe the one officer.

◦ Sentence as given: Rohan is an honest and hardworking officer who has served the department for years.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: "a honest and hardworking officer" — "a" cannot be used before the vowel sound of "honest".

 

• Option 2: "honest and hardworking officer" — a singular countable noun needs an article.

 

• Option 3: "an honest and hardworking officers" — "officers" is plural, and it does not agree with the singular subject "Rohan" or with "an".

 

NOTE

 

• silent "h": an honest man, an honour, an hour; article + adjective(s) + singular noun: a tall and strong man, an honest and hardworking officer.

question: Identify the sentence that correctly uses the indefinite article.
option_1: The architect designed an house with an open courtyard and a small garden.
option_2: The architect designed a house with a open courtyard and a small garden.
option_3: The architect designed a house with an open courtyard and a small garden.
option_4: The architect designed a house with an open courtyard and an small garden.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. The architect designed a house with an open courtyard and a small garden.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Only Option 3 is correct. The choice of "a" or "an" depends on the sound that follows. "House" and "small" begin with consonant sounds (a house, a small), and "open" begins with a vowel sound (an open).

◦ Correct sentence: The architect designed a house with an open courtyard and a small garden.

 

• Each of the other three options contains a different article error, explained below.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: "an house" — "house" begins with a pronounced "h", which is a consonant sound, so "a house" is needed.

 

• Option 2: "a open courtyard" — "open" begins with a vowel sound, so "an open courtyard" is needed.

 

• Option 4: "an small garden" — "small" begins with a consonant sound, so "a small garden" is needed.

 

NOTE

 

• a house, a hotel (pronounced "h"); an open, an old (vowel sounds); an hour, an honest (silent "h").

question:
Choose the most suitable option to replace the highlighted part of the sentence.

 

The tour company organises trips to the Nepal and the Maldives every summer.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Nepal and the Maldives.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The name of a single country takes no article (Nepal), but the name of an island group or a plural name takes "the" (the Maldives). So "the Nepal and the Maldives" must be "Nepal and the Maldives".

◦ Corrected sentence: The tour company organises trips to Nepal and the Maldives every summer.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: "Nepal and Maldives" — "the" is needed before the plural island-group name "the Maldives".

 

• Option 3: "the Nepal and Maldives" — "the" is wrongly used before "Nepal" and wrongly omitted before "Maldives".

 

• Option 4: "the Nepal and the Maldive" — "the" is wrongly used before "Nepal", and "Maldive" is not the correct form of the name.

 

NOTE

 

• no "the": Nepal, India, France; "the": the Maldives, the Philippines, the Netherlands, the United States, the United Kingdom.

question: Select the grammatically correct sentence.
option_1: I saw an owl in the garden. The owl was sitting on a branch.
option_2: I saw owl in the garden. The owl was sitting on a branch.
option_3: I saw an owl in garden. The owl was sitting on a branch.
option_4: I saw a owl in the garden. The owl was sitting on a branch.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. I saw an owl in the garden. The owl was sitting on a branch.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Only Option 1 is correct. "An" is used for the first mention of a singular noun that begins with a vowel sound ("an owl"), and "the" is used for the second mention ("The owl"), because it is now known.

◦ Correct sentence: I saw an owl in the garden. The owl was sitting on a branch.

 

• Each of the other three options contains a different article error, explained below.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 2: "I saw owl" — "owl" is a singular countable noun mentioned for the first time, so it needs "an".

 

• Option 3: "in garden" — "garden" is a singular countable noun, so it needs an article ("in the garden").

 

• Option 4: "a owl" — "owl" begins with a vowel sound, so it takes "an" and not "a".

 

NOTE

 

• first mention — a / an (I saw an owl); second mention — the (The owl flew away).

question: Select the grammatically correct sentence.
option_1: The decision to shut the factory hurt the livelihood of the workers.
option_2: An decision to shut the factory hurt the livelihood of the workers.
option_3: The decision to shut an factory hurt the livelihood of the workers.
option_4: The decision to shut the factory hurt livelihood of the workers.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. The decision to shut the factory hurt the livelihood of the workers.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Only Option 1 is correct. The nouns "decision" and "livelihood" are made specific by the phrases that follow them ("to shut the factory", "of the workers"), so both take "the".

◦ Correct sentence: The decision to shut the factory hurt the livelihood of the workers.

 

• Each of the other three options contains a different article error, explained below.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 2: "An decision" — "decision" begins with a consonant sound, so "an" is wrong.

 

• Option 3: "shut an factory" — "factory" begins with a consonant sound, so "an" is wrong, and the factory is a specific one.

 

• Option 4: "hurt livelihood of the workers" — "livelihood" is specified by "of the workers", so it needs "the".

 

NOTE

 

• the + noun + "of" phrase: the beauty of the park, the livelihood of the workers, the decision of the court.

question: Select the grammatically correct sentence.
option_1: She was given an one-year contract by the company.
option_2: She was given one-year contract by the company.
option_3: She was given a one-year contract by the company.
option_4: She was given a one-year contract by company.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. She was given a one-year contract by the company.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Only Option 3 is correct. "One" is pronounced "wun", which begins with a consonant sound, so it takes "a": "a one-year contract". The company is a specific one, so "the company" is used.

◦ Correct sentence: She was given a one-year contract by the company.

 

• Each of the other three options contains a different article error, explained below.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: "an one-year" — "one" begins with the consonant sound "w", so "a" is needed and not "an".

 

• Option 2: "one-year contract" — a singular countable noun needs an article ("a one-year contract").

 

• Option 4: "by company" — "company" is a specific one here, so it needs "the".

 

NOTE

 

• the "w" sound of "one" takes "a": a one-rupee coin, a one-way street, a once-in-a-lifetime chance.

question: Select the grammatically correct sentence.
option_1: What an exciting match it was!
option_2: What a exciting match it was!
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. What an exciting match it was!.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Only Option 1 is correct. After "What" in an exclamation, the article comes before the adjective and the singular noun, and "exciting" begins with a vowel sound, so the article is "an".

◦ Correct sentence: What an exciting match it was!

 

• Each of the other three options contains a different article error, explained below.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 2: "What a exciting" — "exciting" begins with a vowel sound, so "an" is needed and not "a".

 

• Option 3: "What exciting match" — a singular countable noun after "what" needs an article ("What an exciting match").

 

• Option 4: "Such exciting match" — "such" also needs an article before a singular noun ("Such an exciting match").

 

NOTE

 

• what a / what an + (adjective) + singular noun: What a pity, What an idea; similarly such a / such an.
